formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Sets the spender's VELO allowance over the owner's tokens to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (ERC20Permit.permit -> _approve(owner, spender, value)).
An allowance at max uint256 is never reduced when spent (OZ ERC20 _spendAllowance), so it is truly unlimited.
Uses up the owner's current permit nonce (_useNonce(owner)), which voids any other signed permit with the same nonce.
Anyone holding the signature can submit it until `deadline`; after that it reverts (require(block.timestamp <= deadline)).
formats.shown: The screen says "Authorize spending of tokens". It shows the spender as a raw address, the maximum VELO amount (with "Unlimited" at 2^255 or more), the valid-until date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit has no interpolatedIntent, so the intent line names no token, amount or spender.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json display.formats.Permit: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", and interpolatedIntent is absent (FORMATS.md: interpolatedIntent: null). The value and spender fields have formats and are always visible, so the sentence could include them.
findings.fix: Add "interpolatedIntent": "Allow {spender} to spend up to {value} until {deadline}".

findings.title: Permit shows the spender as a raw hex address, not a resolved name.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json Permit field {"path": "spender", "format": "raw"}. This matches the registry's ERC-2612 permit convention.
findings.fix: Use "format": "addressName" with types ["contract","eoa"] so the wallet can show a known name for the spender.
